div.p: ¶ A goodly interlude of Nature cōpylyd by mayster Henry Medwall chapleyn to the ryght reuerent father in god Iohan Morton somtyme Cardynall and arche byshop of Canterbury⸫

div.head: ¶ The second part •… .
div.l: ¶ I assemble the lyfe of mortall creature
To the allyege agayn a s •… rong town or castell
In whyche there ys myche b •… st endenure
myche warly polycy wyth bysy trauayll
On euery syde whyche par •… e shall prey ayll
By sleyght of ingyns or by strong power
that other to subdue and bryng into daunger
¶ In suche case and maner of condycyon
Is wreched man here in thys lyfe erthly
Whyle he abydeth wythin the garyson
Of the frayll carcas and carynouse body
Whom to impugn laboreth incessantly
the world / the fleshe / the enemy / these thre
Hym to subdue and bryng into captyuyte
¶ And for to shew you what wyse they vs ipugn
Fyrst doth the world geue vs an allectyfe
to couetryches and worldly renown
Wyth other vanyteys that be vsed in thys lyfe
Next that our fleshe whyche euer ys in stryse
agayn our spyryte / doth prouoke and excyte
Ys to accomplyshe our sensuall appetyte
¶ The last of all ys our great enemy
Whyche euer hath vs in contynuall haterede
Of old enkankred malyce and enuy
that he oweth to vs and all the kynrede
Of all the aunceters of whom we do succede
Nor yetcesseth hys malyce vnto thys day
Ys to endaunger in all that he can or may
¶ And certes these our sayd enemyes
Be of theyre nature so myghty and so strong
That hard yt wyll be for vs in any wyse
Agayn them warre or batayll to vnderfong
also our garisons and fortresse to mayntayn long
Agayn theyre ingens wythout spyrytuall grace
We can not performe in no maner case
¶ Wherfore yt ys to vs ryght behouable
Besyly to pray to god that ys immortall
Besechyng hym as he ys mercyable
To haue compassyon and pytye on vs all
And not to suffer vs any wyse to fall
Into suche foly and vtter myschaunce
Is 〈◊〉 theym greue and do 〈◊◊〉
¶ Also yt behoueth on our parte
To fle all suche maner of occasyon
as may be put in fere and Ieoparde
Of theyre dyspleasure in any con ••• cyon
New fangl •… s and c 〈◊◊〉 nyce 〈◊〉
we must forsake in all maner wyse
And acquaynt vs wyth theyre contrar • se
Quia contraria contrariis curantur. &c.
I tell thys tale syr to you
Trustyng that yt be not done in wast
ye remember as I suppose well I now
Now yt ys not fully. in. dayes past
Syth ye me promysed and bound yt fast
From that day forth to be obedyent
unto my counsell and aduysement

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ ye syr so I dyd in very ded
And yet yt ys my mynde and intent
To folow the same haue ye no drede

sp.speaker: Rea.
sp.l: ¶ yf ye do nat your selfe shall repent
Now fare ye well for I must be absent
As for a season / and for your confort
whan so euer ye call me I shall to you resort
sp.stage: ¶ Then he goeth out & Sensua. cometh in.

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ God forbed that euer he com agayn
Iesu how may ye thys lyfe endure
Me semeth yt shuld be to you a great payn
Syth ye be of good complexyon and nature
To forbere the worldly sport and pleasure
As ye haue done now a great seson
and all by the folyshe counsell of reson
¶ Where ys your lusty hart bycom
That serued you so well thys other day
Now so helpe me god and halydom
I haue great maruell how ye may
Lyue in suche mysery / and thys dare I say
wythout ye take some other wayes
By my trouth yt wyll shorten your dayes
¶ And though I say yt that were pyte
For by cryste and ye were gone
Meny a good felow wold make great mone

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Why wepe ye so

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ let me alone
It wyll none other wyse be
and ye saw the sorowfull countenaunce
Of my cumpany your old acquayntaunce
that they make
For your sake
I dare say ye wold mone theym in your mynde
They be so louyng and so kynde
That I am sure
yf ye endure
In thys peuyshe opynyon
It wyll be theyre confessyon
There ys none other remedy
But for sorow they shall dye

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Nay god forbed they shuld so do

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ In fayth wythout ye help therto
There ys none other way

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ I wyll help yt in all that I may
And I wyst by what mene

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ Mary call theym to your cumpany

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ By saynt Ihān I am content
For I may say here to the
Syth I forsoke my lyberte
And dyd to Reson assent
I had neuer mery day
But lyued vnder awe and drede alway
Nothyng to myne intent
Another whyle I wyll me dysport
and to myne old cumpany resort

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ O than shall ye theym confort
and your selfe also
Wote ye who wyll be very glad

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Who

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ Margery

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Why was she sad

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ ye by the masse she was stark mad
Euen for very wo
Whan she hard tell of thys chaunce
And bycause she wold lyue in penaunce
Her sorow for to quenche
She hath entred into a relygyouse place
At the grene frerys hereby

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ ye hase.
Alak good 〈◊〉 wenche
Is yt an house of strayt relygyon

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ ye as any that euer was bygon
Syth the world stode

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Be they close nonnes as other be

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ Close ꝙ a nay nay parde
That gyse were not good
ye must beware of that gere
Nay all ys open that they do there
As open as a gose eye

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ And cometh any man into theyre sellys

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ ye ye god forbede ellys
It ys fre for euery body
And bysyde all thys they be
Ex omni gente cognite
No nacyon they forsake
Wythout yt be beggars goyng by the way
That haue neuer a peny to pay
For that that they do take
¶ And yet can I beggars thyderlede
Where they shalbe for lumpes of brede
Satysfye theyre desyre
Suche drabbes some there be
That requyre none other fe
Nor yet any other hyre

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Be they not wedded as other folke be

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ Wedded quod a no so mot I the
They wyll nottary therfore
they can wed theym selfe alone
Com kys me Ihān gramercy Ione
Thys wed they euer more
And yt ys the more to comend
For yf the woman hap to offend
as yt ys theyre gyse
a man may let her alone wyth sorow
and wed another hore on the morow
Euen of the same wyse

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Forsoth thys ys a noble relygyon
It styrreth me to great deuocyon
For to se that place
Canst thou bryng me thyder well I now

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ ye and yt were myd nyght I make god auow
As dark as euer yt was

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ But where ys bodely lust now

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ Then cometh in bodyly lust wyth hym w. aff.
¶ Mary syr I haue sytten and sought you

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: Thys thre or. iiii. howrys
¶ I make god auow
ye gyue shrewd attendaunce

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: All thys. ii. dayes I coulde not the espy
¶ Syr ye know well that ye and I
Be neuer myche a sonder

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: albe yt I be from you among
¶ And now me semeth thou hast taryed to long

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: whyche ys to me great wonder
¶ Wonder ye parde for an howr or twayn
Forth for a passyng whyle and com agayn
Here ys a sore mater
whan was I so long absent as now
and yet I was for to seke you
at the tother syde of the water
The place that ye wot of parde

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: Vnderstande ye what ye mene

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ ye ye

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Tell me in myne ere

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ Quid est latinum propter le stewys
¶ What laten now thys of the newys
I herd neuer thys ere

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: I trow ye begyn to waxe shamfast
¶ Nay nay hardely that gere ys past
Meny dayes a gon

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: I am as wanton as euer I was
¶ It were almes to hang you ellys by the masse
By the hard necke bon
But wyll ye now go wyth me to a place
and I shall shew you the smorterst place

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: That euer ye saw wyth eyes

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ What thyng ys yt yong or old
¶ What euer yt be yt ys able to be sold

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: It shall lyke you on the best wyse
¶ For my loue let vs some nyght be there
at a banket or a rere supper
and get vs some wanton mete
So we may haue some deynty thyng
yet wold I spende. xx. shyllyng
where so euer I yt get

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ Nay nay wyll ye spende a coyell of crownes
and there shall no gentylman in thys. x. townes
Be better serued than ye
Nor be receyued more honestly
As to an house of bawdry
For a banket or •… nkry
For a dyshe. ii. or thre

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ yes that wyll I spend wyth all myne hart

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ By your leue I wyll depart
To make redy thys gere

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ What now in all thys hast

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ ye for god syr I am a gast
that other knaues wyll come theder
byfore vs and take vp all

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Se there to I pray the

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ So I shall
Ellys fye on all together

sp.speaker: w. aff.
sp.l: ¶ Now wyll margery make great mone
bycause ye com not.

sp.speaker: ¶ Man.
sp.l: ye let her alone
I am not her bond man parde
She hath dysappoynted me or now

sp.speaker: w. aff.
sp.l: ¶ yet on my fayth syr and I were as you
at the leste I wold excuse me
Send her word that ye in no wyse
May thys nyght kepe her promyse
And yf ye do not so
She wyll so morn that as I thynk
Of all thys nyght she wyll slepe no wynk
She shalbe so full of wo

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ ye on my parell take no care
Thys answere wyll I deffar and spare
tyll I be certayn
what answere bodyly lust shall bryng
Of thys other praty new thyng
whan he cometh agayne

sp.speaker: w. aff.
sp.l: ¶ Wyll yt please you that I go to mergery
In your stede

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Mary that were mery
woldyst thou serue me so

sp.speaker: w. aff.
sp.l: ¶ Why syr by my trouth I mene but well

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ ye what thou menyst I can not tell
But that shall thou not do

sp.speaker: w. aff.
sp.l: ¶ In good fayth syr ye may do wurs
For whyle I haue any thyng in my purs
Or any peny to spend
I wyll make her euen suche chere
As I wold myne own wyfe yf she were here
Ellys god defend

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ ye I thanke the for thy good wyll
But as for that chere kepe yt styll
Tyll I call theron

sp.speaker: w. aff.
sp.l: ¶ By god syr for good loue I spake yt
And now that I se ye wyll not take yt
I shall let yt alone

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ How now hast thou bene yender away

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ ye syr.

sp.speaker: ¶ Man.
sp.l: Et que nouellys

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ Ie nescey
I could not speke wyth her
No wyth none of her folkys

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Not wyth one

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ No they be a slepe euerychone
All that euer dwell there

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ How knowest thou wether they be a slepe or n •…

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ Mary she her selfe told me so
whan I rapped at the dore

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ It semeth she was not a slepe than

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ No she was a bed wyth a strange man

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ A myschefe on her hore
I wold this fyre wer i her tayll I make god auow

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ That nedeth not she ys hote I now
It were more almes to get
Some cold water her fyre to quenche
I tell you yt ys as warm a wenche
As any in all thys strete
I supposed I had angred her yll

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ How so

sp.speaker: bodyly
sp.l: ¶ For I rang her a knyll
That waked her from her slepe
I gaue her a pele for her frendys soulys
a man myght haue hard the noys from poulys
To the farthest ende of chepe
She saw that I wold not feace but knok
And rap styll at the gate
She opened a wyndow and put forth her hed
Hens. xl. d. ꝙ she. Iak noble ys a bed
Thys 〈◊〉 ye come •… o 〈◊〉
I ha standeth the wynd so cold quod I
〈◊〉 . q. tytle we haue a bry
Thys gere goeth all wyde
And so I cam thens a great pace
tyll I cam hyder / lo thys ys the case
Haue I not well hyde

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Well man there ys no more to do
that we cannot haue we must forgo
there ys none other remedy
Lo worldly affeccyon now mayst thou se
Thy counsell was nought that thou gauest me

sp.speaker: w. aff.
sp.l: ¶ No more yt was truely

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ ye I told the asmyche byfore
It ys good to be sure euer more
therfore now let vs go
And resorte agayn to our old hostes
that ys the best way now as I gesse

sp.speaker: w. aff.
sp.l: ¶ ye hardely do so
sp.stage: ¶ Then they thre go out & Pryde cometh in.

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ Syrs remember ye that thys other day
Man promysed me euen in thys stede
that I shuld wyth hym dwell and now I here say
The wylde worm ys com into hys hed
So that by reason only he ys led
It may well be so / but I am sure
that Reason shall not alway wyth hym endure
¶ Me thynketh that Sensua. doth not hys parte
accordyng to the duety of hys offyce
for no body can better torn a mannys hart
Nor yet a redyer mean deuyse
to put away suche folyshe fantasyse
than Sensualyte yf he lust to assay
for he ys chyef ruler whan Reason ys away

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ ye / a ruler wyll I be though Reason say nay

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ Ah Sensualyte welcom by thys day
what tydyngys good

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ ye by my fay
as good as can be told
I haue brought thys man to hys old gyse

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ Hast thou so

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ ye on warantyse

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ Now forsoth I gyue the pryk and pryse
Of thys tydyngys I am glad and fayn
But shall I be welcom to hym agayn
and all our cumpany

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ ye hardely
as welcom as euer ye ware byfore

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ Goddys blessyng haue thyn hart therfore
thus am I in thy det more and more

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ Iapes why say ye so

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ for I speke yt after my mynde
thou art to me alway so kynde
But where shall I our mayster fynde
to hym wyll I go

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ He ys besy harke in your ere
wyth lytell margery ye wote where
And as sone as I had brought hym there
I cam my way a pace
and bycause he shuld not be alone
I left wyth hym worldly affeccyon
and other erand had I none
Now to thys place
but euen to shew you what ys done
and from hens I must anone
for to seke an other companyon
to gyue attendaunce

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ Who ys that

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ Mary glotony
Our mayster calleth for hym besyly
Sawyst thou hym not

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ No certaynly
To my remembraunce

sp.speaker: sensua
sp.l: ¶ I must go seeke hym wythout any taryeng
But Pryde I warn you of one thyng
Whyle I thynk theron
whan my mayster and ye shall mete
In any wyse se that ye hym grete
In the old fassyon
And make as though ye know nothyng
Of hys dyuers and varyable dealyng
Kepe that in your brest
ye can not do hym more dyspleasure
Than therof to make reporture
Therfore let yt rest

〈◊◊◊〉
•… gh treson

sp.speaker: •… de
sp.l: ¶ 〈◊〉 g •… ad ye warn me thus in seson
〈◊◊〉 the better were
B •… th •… s warnyng I shalbe wyse
And do as ye me aduertyse
take therof no ca •…

sp.speaker: ¶ Slouth.
sp.l: ¶ Wyll ye be wyse quod a / mary that ys a thyng
By god ye had nede to haue better warnyng
Or ye bryng that about

sp.speaker: •… de
sp.l: ¶ What brother Slouth fro whens comyst thou

sp.speaker: •… h.
sp.l: ¶ Streyght fro my bed I make god auow
Myne eyes be almost out
for lak of slepe / but thys syr to you
Me thought ye called me slouth ryght now
Pece no more of that
I haue a new name as well as ye

sp.speaker: •… de
sp.l: ¶ What ys that / ease

sp.speaker: •… h.
sp.l: ¶ ye parde
But yt forceth not
whyle our mayster ys not present
Bytwene vs twayn I am content
Call me what ye wyll
But where ys our mayster

sp.speaker: •… de
sp.l: ¶ Wotest thou nere

sp.speaker: •… h.
sp.l: ¶ No

sp.speaker: •… de
sp.l: ¶ No more do I

sp.speaker: •… h.
sp.l: ¶ There there there
Thou shalt dwell wyth me styll
Thou art as good a wayter as I

sp.speaker: •… de
sp.l: ¶ I shrew the better of vs both hardely
But surely we do not well
we shall not contynue wyth yonder man
but we awayte better now and than
Therfore by my counsell
Let vs twayn go together
To seeke our mayster

sp.speaker: •… h.
sp.l: ¶ But wotyst thou whether
we shall now go
To fynde our mayster

sp.speaker: •… de
sp.l: ¶ I shall assay
Thou shalt se me gesse the way
And happely fynde hym to
Now must I to the stewes as fast as I may
to •… ech thys gentylman but syrs I say
Can any man here tell me the way
For I cam neuer there
ye know the way parde of old
I pray the tell me whyche way shall I hold
wyll ye se thys horson cocold
I trow he cannot here
Now yt were almes to clap the on the crown
sp.stage: ¶ Then cometh in man and worldly aff.

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ Why be there any cocoldys in town

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ ye I durst hold theron my gown
that there be a score
but for god I cry you mercy
for by my sayth I wyst you not so ny
Had I wyst yt I ensure you faythfully
that word I wold haue forbore

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ No force hardely yt toucheth not me
But wurshyp tell me where haue ye be
Me thynketh long syth I you se

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ Syr yt ys no maruell
Bad ye not me the last day
To go puruey for your aray
And ye remember well

sp.speaker: Man.
sp.l: ¶ ye for god haue ye done the same

sp.speaker: Pryde
sp.l: ¶ ye by the rode ellys were I to blame
All thyng ys redy in payn of shame
Ellys I quyte me yll
The tayler told me yester nyght
that all your garmentys were redy dyght
